scoreRule: 1 point per correct MC item; 10 points maximum; local provisional grade only
description: Ten newly written comprehension, interpretation and situational transfer questions; pending independent teacher review.

questions.q: What problem makes Tom depend on Mia's help?
choices: He is at work and cannot shop before the party.
He does not know where his cousin lives.
He has lost the money for the birthday present.
He cannot attend the birthday celebration.
questions.explanation: Tom's shift at the bike shop prevents him from buying a gift himself.

questions.q: What does Mia's reaction to the book suggest?
choices: Eva has asked for another book this year.
Past gifts can tell you what someone may not enjoy.
Mia thinks all books are too expensive.
The library refuses to sell presents.
questions.explanation: Mia remembers that Eva never opened the book she received last year.

questions.q: Why does a concert ticket fail as a present?
choices: Eva dislikes music when she is climbing.
The concert is taking place at the bike shop.
There are no tickets left for Eva's favourite band.
Tom will be away for the whole next month.
questions.explanation: Tickets have sold out, so the friends need another idea.

questions.q: How does Mia's suggestion solve the budget problem?
choices: It allows Tom to borrow expensive headphones.
It gives Eva a concert ticket for free.
It costs more but the shop will pay the difference.
A two-visit climbing card fits within thirty euros.
questions.explanation: Mia identifies a gift costing twenty-eight euros, within Tom's limit.

questions.q: Why does Tom respond enthusiastically to the climbing-centre idea?
choices: Eva has never shown any interest in climbing.
Eva already finds the school's climbing wall too easy.
The centre is closing after the party.
Mia promises a new bicycle as well.
questions.explanation: The new climbing centre matches Eva's interests and offers a new challenge.

questions.q: What does Mia's final comment about the phone calendar imply?
choices: The party has been moved to next year.
A phone is necessary to enter the climbing centre.
Eva wants a new calendar instead of a present.
Tom should plan ahead to avoid forgetting birthdays.
questions.explanation: Mia jokes about Tom's last-minute problem and recommends remembering next year.

questions.q: Why does Tom offer to buy a birthday card himself?
choices: He can contribute something while Mia buys the gift.
He wants to change the gift back to a book.
He needs to write a card for his manager.
The climbing centre requires a handwritten letter.
questions.explanation: Tom divides the tasks so both friends help prepare Eva's present.

questions.q: You have a limited budget and concert tickets are unavailable. What should you do?
choices: Buy tickets at any price even if they are sold out.
Choose the same unused gift as last year.
Find another activity linked to the person's interests.
Give up without asking what the person likes.
questions.explanation: Mia moves from an unavailable concert to another gift related to Eva's hobbies.

questions.q: What is the most helpful message Tom could send after Friday?
choices: Ask Mia to buy an even more expensive gift.
Thank Mia and repay the money he owes her.
Tell Eva not to use the climbing card.
Refuse to help write the birthday card.
questions.explanation: The arrangement depends on Mia buying the present and Tom paying her back.

questions.q: Why would headphones be a poor choice in this situation?
choices: Eva has explicitly refused to listen to music.
All headphone shops are closed for the year.
They cannot be wrapped as a birthday present.
Good ones cost more than Tom can spend.
questions.explanation: Mia compares the cost of quality headphones with Tom's budget.
